faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: We believe lottery analysis should be accessible to everyone. While some desktop lottery software costs $100-300 upfront and competitor subscriptions charge $7+/month, we keep our prices low — less than the cost of a single lottery ticket. Our goal is to help you play smarter, not drain your potential winnings on expensive tools.
faq.a2: We analyze historical lottery draw data using statistical methods including frequency analysis, Wilson confidence intervals, and Monte Carlo simulations to calculate probabilities.
faq.q3: How often is the data updated?
faq.a3: Lottery draw data is typically updated within 24 hours of each draw. The exact timing may vary depending on the lottery.
faq.a4: See our subscription page for details on each tier. Higher tiers unlock longer historical data ranges and advanced analytics features.
faq.q5: Is this a guarantee to win?
faq.a5: No. Lottery results are completely random. Our analysis shows historical patterns and statistical probabilities, but past performance does not predict future results.
faq.a6: When multiple numbers have the same historical frequency, they're considered 'tied' - equally likely based on past data. We show all tied numbers together so you don't miss any equally probable options.
faq.a7: Hot numbers appear more frequently than expected in recent draws. Cold numbers appear less often than expected. Normal numbers are close to their expected frequency. This helps identify current trends in the data.
faq.q8: How does the app suggest which numbers to play?
faq.a8: We analyze historical draw data and show the numbers with the highest appearance frequency. The number of suggestions matches what you need to pick for each lottery (e.g., 5 main numbers for EuroJackpot). Numbers with identical frequencies are shown together as ties.
faq.a9: We support 22 lotteries across 5 regions: Estonia, United Kingdom, United States, Spain, and Ireland. This includes popular games like EuroJackpot, EuroMillions, Powerball, Mega Millions, and many more.
faq.q10: Can I analyze data from specific time periods?
faq.a10: Yes! You can select custom date ranges to focus your analysis on specific periods. This helps you see how number patterns have changed over time.
faq.q11: What statistical methods do you use?
faq.a11: We use multiple statistical methods including frequency analysis, Wilson confidence intervals, trend analysis, and Monte Carlo simulations. For detailed explanations, visit our <methodology>Statistical Methodology</methodology> page.
faq.q12: What's the difference between subscription tiers?
faq.a12:
Free — 2 months of data with basic frequency analysis.
Pro — 2 years of data, plus trends, confidence intervals, and deviation metrics.
Premium — 5 years of data with all advanced analytics including Markov chains, pair analysis, and seasonal patterns.

methodology.title: Statistical Methodology
methodology.subtitle: How we analyze lottery data
methodology.intro: LottoLens uses a combination of statistical methods to analyze historical lottery data. Our goal is to help you understand patterns and probabilities, while always remembering that lottery results are fundamentally random.

frequencyAnalysis.title: Frequency Analysis
frequencyAnalysis.description: We count how many times each number has appeared in historical draws and calculate its frequency as a percentage. This shows which numbers have been drawn more or less often than average.
frequencyAnalysis.helps: Identifies numbers that appear more or less frequently than expected based on historical data.

wilsonConfidenceInterval.title: Wilson Confidence Interval
wilsonConfidenceInterval.description: This statistical method calculates a range within which the true probability of a number likely falls, accounting for sample size. It's more accurate than simple percentages, especially with smaller datasets.
wilsonConfidenceInterval.helps: Provides a reliable probability range with a confidence level, giving you a more accurate picture than raw percentages.

hotColdNumbers.title: Hot & Cold Numbers
hotColdNumbers.description: Numbers are classified as 'hot' (appearing more than expected), 'cold' (appearing less than expected), or 'normal' based on their deviation from the expected frequency.
hotColdNumbers.helps: Quickly identifies which numbers are currently on streaks or due for appearances based on recent trends.

trendAnalysis.title: Trend Analysis
trendAnalysis.description: We analyze how each number's frequency has changed over time, looking at whether it's increasing, decreasing, or remaining stable across different time periods.
trendAnalysis.helps: Shows whether a number's appearance rate is changing, helping you spot emerging patterns.

streaksGaps.title: Streaks & Gaps Analysis
streaksGaps.description: We track consecutive appearances (streaks) and consecutive absences (gaps) for each number, including the longest streak, longest gap, and average time between appearances.
streaksGaps.helps: Reveals patterns in how numbers cluster together or spread apart over time.

markovChain.title: Markov Chain Analysis
markovChain.description: This method analyzes what typically happens after a number appears or doesn't appear. It calculates transition probabilities to see if numbers tend to repeat, alternate, or behave randomly.
markovChain.helps: Predicts the likelihood of a number appearing based on its previous state (appeared or didn't appear).

autocorrelation.title: Autocorrelation Analysis
autocorrelation.description: We check if a number's appearances are related to its appearances in previous draws. This detects whether numbers tend to cluster (appear together), disperse evenly, or appear randomly.
autocorrelation.helps: Detects hidden patterns that might indicate non-random behavior in number sequences.

pairAnalysis.title: Number Pair Analysis
pairAnalysis.description: We analyze which numbers frequently appear together and which ones rarely coincide. Using lift calculations, we determine if pairs occur more or less often than expected by chance.
pairAnalysis.helps: Identifies companion numbers that tend to appear together and pairs that seem to avoid each other.

monteCarlo.title: Monte Carlo Simulation
monteCarlo.description: We run thousands of simulated lottery draws to establish what 'normal' random behavior looks like. Your actual results are then compared against this simulated baseline.
monteCarlo.helps: Validates whether observed patterns are statistically significant or just normal random variation.

seasonalPatterns.title: Seasonal Pattern Detection
seasonalPatterns.description: We analyze whether certain numbers appear more frequently on specific days of the week or months of the year, looking for any temporal patterns in the data.
seasonalPatterns.helps: Reveals if numbers have any correlation with calendar patterns like weekdays or seasons.

disclaimer.title: Important Reminder
disclaimer.content: While these statistical methods provide interesting insights into historical patterns, lottery results are fundamentally random. Past performance does not predict future results. Use this information for entertainment and educational purposes only. Please gamble responsibly.
